trans-unit.source: When filling out the form, a mandatory absence type is required to be selected, so that it provides full context to the reason why. Here's a list of all available absence types:

trans-unit.source: Vacation — Planned time off approved in advance, used for rest, travel, or personal leisure.
Personal — Short-term leave for attending to personal matters that cannot be handled outside working hours.
Parental — Leave taken for the birth, adoption, or fostering of a child, including time to support early caregiving.
Sabbatical — Extended leave granted for personal growth, research, travel, or rejuvenation, typically based on tenure or company policy.
Educational — Approved leave to pursue training, coursework, or professional development programs that support career growth.
Sick — Time off due to illness, injury, or medical appointments that prevent an employee from performing their duties.
Family Emergency — Unplanned absence required to address urgent or unexpected situations affecting immediate family members.
Bereavement — Leave taken in the event of the death of a family member to allow for grieving, funeral arrangements, or related matters.
Jury Duty — Legally mandated absence to serve as a juror or participate in related court proceedings.
Military — Leave required for military service, training, or related obligations as mandated by law.
Unpaid — Approved absence taken without compensation when other leave types are unavailable or not applicable.
Unauthorized Absence — Time away from work without prior approval or valid justification, not in compliance with company policy.
Absences can only be approved by the owner or any other manager responsible for this section. This operation can be done in the absences grid status column with the thumb icons.

Welcome to Shift Scheduler! This guide will walk you through the essential steps to begin using the application and understand its core workflow.
To start using Shift Scheduler, you’ll first need to create or join a work entity. You can do this by:
Creating a New Entity — If you’re setting up Shift Scheduler for your organization, select the option to create a new work entity and provide the necessary details.
Joining an Existing Entity — If your organization is already using Shift Scheduler, request an invitation from your administrator to join the existing work entity.

When you login in, the dashboard provides quick access to your schedules, team information, shift templates, rules, absences, and other relevant information of your work entities. Each section is designed to keep your scheduling operations clear and organized.
As a manager, you can add your team members to the system. You can define their roles, availability, and permissions, ensuring Shift Scheduler has accurate data to work with.
Shift Scheduler relies on templates and rules to build schedules efficiently. Define shift types, durations, requirements, and constraints so the system knows how to assign work properly.
As a worker, you can submit absence requests for your manager to approve. These absences are taken into account for generating the required schedules.

With your team, shifts, and rules in place, you’re ready to generate your first schedule. Simply choose a time period, apply your templates, resolve conflicts if needed, and publish the schedule to your team.

Features Overview — Discover all the tools available to you
Tutorials — Step-by-step instructions for common tasks
Rules — Learn how to build constraints that guide scheduling

When adding layers of rules to your organization, conflicts can occur due to their similar nature between them. In this current version of schedule generation, certain rule types have priorities over others.
For example, setting a maximum amount of workers per shift of 10, will prioritize higher over required amount of skillset per shift that can specify 6 workers of Skill X and 6 of Skill Y.
Here is the list of rule types ordered by priority from highest to lowest, that can enter in conflict:

When creating rules, keep in mind that the more rules you add, the more restrictions the schedule generator will have to comply with. This can lead to situations where no valid schedule can be generated due to conflicting or overly restrictive rules.
It's advisable to start with a basic set of rules and gradually add more as needed, testing the schedule generation after each addition to ensure feasibility.
Some rule types cover specific scenarios. Recommend the use of a mix of generic and specific rule types for better results.
Engage with your workforce to understand their needs and preferences, and consider incorporating their feedback into the rule-setting process to enhance satisfaction and compliance.
Regularly review and update the rules to reflect any changes in operational needs or workforce capabilities.
This section provides information about managing schedules within the application. You can create, edit, and delete schedules as needed, either as an automated process or a manual task.
You can view schedules in two different formats:
Several general actions can be performed on schedules:
In "List View", pressing a table cell where the worker and a specific date meet, will show a menu of actions that can be performed specific to a worker or schedule. Here's a list of what it can do:
These actions are covered more in depth, in the "Manual Scheduling" section of this page.
Schedules can be managed with the existing automated process or through the various manual processes that the application has to offer.

The automated scheduling feature allows users to set up schedules that are generated based on predefined rules and criteria. This can help streamline the scheduling process and ensure consistency across different time periods.
For this operation to work, members, shifts and rule configurations already have to be in place. Once that is done, access the Schedules page of your work entity and press "Create Schedule" button.
This will open the Create Schedule Window where it will presented with the following options:
Start Date — Sets the start date to where the scheduling process will begin.
End Date — Sets the end date to where the scheduling process will end.
Single Role Responsibility — Determines if a worker will be assigned to a single skill responsibility when assigned to a shift entry.
Clear Existing Schedule — When checked, it will create the schedule from scratch, removing any existing previous entries, before creating the new schedule.
Filterable — Shows the list of members, shifts and rules that the user can select to filter its application on the schedule generation.

When pressing the filterable button, tabbed pages for members, shifts and rules will appear. For each one, you will have a checkbox that you can click to specify what you want to use for your schedule generation.
Once everything is set, press the "Create" button that is presented at the bottom of the page.
This will trigger a warning window to confirm all of the selections, requiring therefore a confirmation.

After confirming, the system will process the request and generate the schedule based on the provided criteria. Depending on the size of the dataset and complexity of the rules, this may take some time.

Manual scheduling provides users with the flexibility to create and adjust schedules as needed. This is particularly useful for handling unique situations or last-minute changes that may not be accommodated by automated processes.

You can view daily schedules in both view modes. In Calendar mode, you select the colored dots that exist. In List mode, clicking on a specific cell of the table will show a menu of options where you can select the "View Day Schedule". The following view will appear:
This view will show the shift entries that a specific worker is assigned to. If there is a more than one entry, an option will appear to switch events. Here it specifies:
Event Name — The name of the event which will always be the shift name.
Start/End — The start and end date and time of the shift.
Participants — A list of all participants in this entry and skills assigned to them.
Manage Day Schedule is an option that the manager can use when he wants to be more hands on. When clicked, the following window will appear:

The manager can create schedule entries for its shifts, who participates in them and their roles. To start, if there are no entries, we select a shift and press the "Add Entry" button. Otherwise, you can select existing entries.

Once an entry is created/selected, a list of available members will appear on left column. You can select one or more workers and then use one of 4 buttons that exist in the middle column, efectively assigning members to the schedule entry.
Removes selected workers from the entry
Assigns selected workers to the entry
Assigns all available workers to the entry

For each assigned worker, you can also specify the skill that he will be using for this entry. By default, all workers skills will already be present, but there will be cancel icon that allows for the removal of that skill. This is subject to change if required, for a add icon with "Add Skill".
Once that happens, a window will appear to select any skill that isnt currently active. Pressing "Add Skill" button will add the skill again to the worker.
Once everything is set, press the "Save" button at the bottom right of the page to save all changes made.

One quick way to add worker to a specific shift, navigate to the desired date and worker in the schedule view. Click on the corresponding cell to open the action menu, then select "Assign Shift". A submenu will appear with a list of available shifts. Click on the desired shift to assign it to the worker for that day.

One of the tools created for workers who are part of the work entity rotation, is to create a rotation cycle. The intent is for the worker to set the rotation from a range period. When pressing "Start Rotation Cycle" option, it will store the worker and the start date of the rotation cycle, allowing the user to select when the rotation cycle ends.
Pressing "Cancel Rotation" will clear the previously saved start date and worker references
When pressing "End Rotation Cycle" in a specific end date, the application will take both dates and worker references to assign the worker in a rotation cycle from that interval range.
This option will clear all assignments that a worker has on the selected date.
This will remove all employee assignments from the current range dates that is current selected.
Setting up your shifts is a critical and required step into creating your schedules.
This guide walks you through the steps required to add a new shift in Shift Scheduler.
To begin, choose the option to "Add Shift" on the top of the page.
To begin, the shift will require the following information:
Shift Name — A descriptive name for the shift (e.g., "Morning Shift");
Shift Color — An optional color to visually distinguish this shift in the schedule. If not assigned, a random color will be selected;

Shift Alias — Alias is meant to be used as an acronym for the shift, 1 to 3 letters maximum. This will be useful to visualize in the schedule what entry was assigned to the worker (e.g., "Morning Shift" with the alias "M");
Start Time: — The time the shift begins;
Shift Duration — The time duration of said shift;
Description - Descriptive information regarding said shift, or any notes that the manager wished to associate with this entry.

Alternatively, you can choose a template from the selection below the form, to prefill the values with existing ones. This will save you time if you are satisfied with pre-existing options or to use some as baseline of what you want.
You can add one or more breaks to your shift by clicking the "Add Break" button.
You will then be presented with the Add Shift Break popup. From there, the manager can proceed in two ways:
Create from Scratch — Manually fill out the break form fields with the following:
Break Type — Specify from a list of possible values, the type of break it is (e.g., "Lunch Break", "Smoke Break", etc.);
Break Start Time — The time where the break begins;
Break Duration — The time duration of the break;

Included in the Shift — Flag that indicates whether the break is expected to occur within the shift duration and to take that into account when creating the schedule entries and when they end (e.g., "Morning Shift" with 8 hours duration that start at 09:00. If this shift has a "Lunch Break" that lasts an hour and flagged as "Included in the Shift", the schedule entry will start at 09:00 and ends at 18:00, for it has 8 hours of shift duration, plus the hour break.);
Is Time Flexible — Flag that indicates internally to the work entity that, even though there is a specific time of when to take the break, its flexible to occur at another point in time.
Based on Template — Choose from pre-configured break templates to quickly apply standard break settings, either to apply it to the letter, or to use as baseline for what you wish to create.
Once added, the shift breaks will appear in the list below the "Add Break" button, where you can edit or delete them as needed.
After completing all required fields and adding breaks as needed, click Create to complete the shift creation process.
Once created, the new shift will appear in the shifts list, ready to be assigned to workers and used in scheduling.
Some work entities may require workers to work within a certain rotation cycle. This can also be set within the shift management page, by adding rotation entries in the "Set Rotation Entry" button.
From there, the Shift Rotation popup will appear, where you can submit:
Shift — You select from the list of shifts that you created;
Leave — You choose to signal a mandatory leave for a specific period of time.
Once added, the rotation entries will appear in the list below the "Set Rotation Entry" button, where you can edit the rotation order or delete them as needed.
